collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A villager whose new roof leaks comes back to the old hut to stay a few nights: make a joke of it, or just say thank you.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) moved into (his/her) own hut last season. This morning, after a night of rain pouring through the roof onto (his/her) face, (he/she) has come back to (his/her) old hut with a wet sleeping mat and an embarrassed expression, to ask if (he/she) can stay until the roof is fixed. Just for a few nights. (He/she) is a grown villager. It shouldn't feel this awkward.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Missed us already?" someone says, and (name1) laughs, and the awkwardness goes. (He/she) stays four nights. It's cozy and loud and nobody lets (him/her) do the washing. When the roof is fixed, (he/she) goes home, and the old hut feels quiet without (him/her) again.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) says thank you, rolls out the mat in (his/her) old spot, and goes quietly back to sleep. Nobody makes a fuss. That's the best part. A few days later the roof is fixed and (he/she) moves back out, carrying a bundle of food nobody admits to having packed.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only
